scope: TanStack Start v1 React documentation, with TanStack Router. Experimental Server Components are qualified separately; this is not the Solid adapter review.

ssr.note: Start integrates React SSR, streaming, hydration and Suspense with its router. This does not imply experimental React Server Components are enabled.

streaming.note: Start integrates React SSR, streaming, hydration and Suspense with its router. This does not imply experimental React Server Components are enabled.

suspense.note: Start integrates React SSR, streaming, hydration and Suspense with its router. This does not imply experimental React Server Components are enabled.

client.note: Start integrates React SSR, streaming, hydration and Suspense with its router. This does not imply experimental React Server Components are enabled.

ssg.note: The build plugin can crawl/enumerate routes and generate static HTML. Dynamic server functions are unavailable on static-only hosting.

csr.note: Route-level ssr:false disables server rendering; normal client navigation still loads and renders through the router.

serverOnly.note: Server Components require an explicit experimental RSC plugin setup. Ordinary server functions are supported without enabling RSC.
serverOnly.label: Experimental RSC

partialRendering.note: Not established in the reviewed TanStack Start rendering guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

routing.note: Start integrates TanStack Router's nested routes/layouts, parameters, navigation and loader prefetching.

layouts.note: Start integrates TanStack Router's nested routes/layouts, parameters, navigation and loader prefetching.

dynamicRoutes.note: Start integrates TanStack Router's nested routes/layouts, parameters, navigation and loader prefetching.

parallelRoutes.note: Not established in the reviewed TanStack Start routing guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

interceptedRoutes.note: Not established in the reviewed TanStack Start routing guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

prefetch.note: Start integrates TanStack Router's nested routes/layouts, parameters, navigation and loader prefetching.

softNavigation.note: The integrated TanStack Router updates route UI and browser history without a reload; reloadDocument explicitly requests document navigation. Pending state, loaders and preloading have separate controls.
softNavigation.label: TanStack Router

viewTransitions.note: Router viewTransition/defaultViewTransition coordinate document.startViewTransition during navigation, including transition types. It is opt-in and depends on browser support; animation CSS and reduced-motion behavior remain app-owned.
viewTransitions.label: TanStack Router

redirects.note: Start integrates TanStack Router's nested routes/layouts, parameters, navigation and loader prefetching.

serverData.note: createServerFn provides typed server handlers callable from route loaders and clients, with middleware and input validation.

clientData.note: Router loaders cache and deduplicate reads, preload destinations and invalidate route data. The route cache is coarser than TanStack Query and is not a durable server cache.

requestDedupe.note: Router loaders cache and deduplicate reads, preload destinations and invalidate route data. The route cache is coarser than TanStack Query and is not a durable server cache.

persistentCache.note: Not established in the reviewed TanStack Start data guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

invalidation.note: Router loaders cache and deduplicate reads, preload destinations and invalidate route data. The route cache is coarser than TanStack Query and is not a durable server cache.

isr.note: Not established in the reviewed TanStack Start data guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

apiRoutes.note: Server routes handle HTTP methods and standard Request/Response bodies, including multipart data. Durable file storage is application/provider-owned.

httpErrors.note: Start combines Router notFound handling with server routes and response-status helpers. Use an explicit Response or setResponseStatus for application HTTP errors rather than relying on a rendered error component alone. Decide failures before the SSR response headers are sent; errors discovered later in a stream cannot replace the committed HTTP status.
httpErrors.label: Router / server response status

actions.note: createServerFn provides typed server handlers callable from route loaders and clients, with middleware and input validation.

forms.note: Server functions accept form data and input validation, with ordinary form submission as a documented transport.

assessment.summary: Form transport, validation, pending feedback and optimistic state are separate behaviors; the progressive-forms and optimistic-updates rows review the latter contracts explicitly.
strengths: Server functions accept form data and input validation, with ordinary form submission as a documented transport.
tradeoffs: Do not infer a no-JavaScript submission path, automatic validation, accessible field errors or rollback merely from the ability to receive FormData.

middleware.note: Composable request and server-function middleware supports shared checks and typed context.

cookies.note: Request-scoped getCookie/setCookie/deleteCookie helpers support session-token cookies. Identity storage, lookup and revocation are application/auth-library responsibilities.

cssModules.note: Start discovers route CSS Modules in the build graph and links their scoped stylesheets during SSR and client navigation.

scopedCss.note: Start discovers route CSS Modules in the build graph and links their scoped stylesheets during SSR and client navigation.

tailwind.note: The guide integrates Tailwind's external build plugin and generated stylesheet.
tailwind.label: Tailwind

cssInJs.note: Not established in the reviewed TanStack Start styling guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

images.note: Not established in the reviewed TanStack Start assets guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

fonts.note: Not established in the reviewed TanStack Start assets guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

scripts.note: Not established in the reviewed TanStack Start assets guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

assetPipeline.note: TanStack Start integrates a bundler-managed client asset graph, including hashed production chunks and SSR asset URL mapping. Its CDN asset URL hook can remap generated URLs. Assets must enter the build graph; copying a file to public/ does not automatically fingerprint it.
assetPipeline.label: Bundler-managed assets

staticAssets.note: Files in public are served at their public paths; imported build assets are processed by the configured bundler. For example, the SEO guide documents automatic serving of public/robots.txt. Public files do not gain hashed filenames merely by being copied.
staticAssets.label: Public directory / bundler

metadata.note: A route head function returns titles, metadata and links and can read loader data; HeadContent renders matched-route head output.

assessment.summary: Typed route head output with explicit nested-route deduplication and loader-data access.
strengths: A child title or same-name/property meta tag replaces the inherited entry.
Head output is loaded and unloaded with route visibility.
tradeoffs: Composition happens at tag level, rather than merging structured SEO objects.
Title templates and more complex inherited arrays require application composition.

dynamicMetadata.note: A route head function returns titles, metadata and links and can read loader data; HeadContent renders matched-route head output.

metadataInheritance.note: Nested-route head entries deduplicate titles and meta tags by semantic name/property; the last/deepest matching tag wins. This is tag-level composition, not recursive SEO-object merging.

metadataOverrides.note: Nested-route head entries deduplicate titles and meta tags by semantic name/property; the last/deepest matching tag wins. This is tag-level composition, not recursive SEO-object merging.

titleTemplates.note: Titles can be composed from matched route data. An inherited template/absolute-reset field API is not established; composition is application code.
titleTemplates.label: Route-data composition

socialImages.note: Not established in the reviewed TanStack Start metadata guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

sitemaps.note: Build-plugin sitemap generation integrates with prerender crawling and an explicit canonical host.

robots.note: A documented public/robots.txt convention serves crawler directives automatically, or a server route can generate the response. The application authors the directives; a typed directive-builder API is not required by this feature definition.
robots.label: Static convention / server route

markdown.note: The documented TanStack Markdown React renderer works during SSR and browser navigation.
markdown.label: TanStack Markdown

collections.note: Not established in the reviewed TanStack Start content guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

draftMode.note: Not established in the reviewed TanStack Start content guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

translations.note: Not established in the reviewed TanStack Start i18n guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

localeRouting.note: Not established in the reviewed TanStack Start i18n guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

localeFormatting.note: Not established in the reviewed TanStack Start i18n guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

auth.note: The guide integrates named providers/libraries such as Better Auth, Clerk and WorkOS; applications choose and configure one.
auth.label: Auth integration

csp.note: Router ssr.nonce lets generated SSR tags carry an application-supplied request nonce; HeadContent also applies it to inlined styles. The application must generate the nonce and matching CSP response header.
csp.label: Application-configured CSP

cspNonce.note: Router ssr.nonce lets generated SSR tags carry an application-supplied request nonce; HeadContent also applies it to inlined styles. The application must generate the nonce and matching CSP response header.
cspNonce.label: SSR nonce option

csrf.note: createCsrfMiddleware enforces browser-origin checks for server functions. It is automatic without a custom src/start.ts; custom start configuration must register it explicitly.

environment.note: Server/client environment boundaries and runtime-aware per-request secret reads are documented; returned values can still expose secrets.

types.note: TypeScript routes/server functions and the Vite/Rsbuild workflow support typed application development and hot updates.

hmr.note: TypeScript routes/server functions and the Vite/Rsbuild workflow support typed application development and hot updates.

cli.note: TypeScript routes/server functions and the Vite/Rsbuild workflow support typed application development and hot updates.

bundleAnalysis.note: Not established in the reviewed TanStack Start tooling guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

unitTests.note: Not established in the reviewed TanStack Start testing guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

e2eTests.note: Not established in the reviewed TanStack Start testing guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

observability.note: The guide documents Sentry instrumentation; request middleware can also add app-owned logging.
observability.label: Sentry

errorHandling.note: Router error components and default/per-route boundaries render fallback UI for failed routes.

serverHosting.note: The overview documents deployment to server and worker runtimes; runtime-specific dependencies must match the target.

subpathProxy.note: TanStack Router’s basepath rebases route matching and generated navigation. Start’s bundler asset base and deployment adapter must be configured consistently, including the public origin behind a proxy. Router basepath alone does not establish that assets and server endpoints are all mounted correctly.
subpathProxy.label: Router base; deployment setup

staticHosting.note: The build plugin can crawl/enumerate routes and generate static HTML. Dynamic server functions are unavailable on static-only hosting.

containers.note: Not established in the reviewed TanStack Start deployment guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

edgeHosting.note: The overview documents deployment to server and worker runtimes; runtime-specific dependencies must match the target.

orm.note: The database guide points to external libraries such as Drizzle and Prisma. Their query, migration and transaction APIs belong to those libraries.
orm.label: Drizzle / Prisma

assessment.summary: An ORM/query API establishes a data-access surface, not identical relationship loading, N+1 detection, migration or encryption behavior.
strengths: The database guide points to external libraries such as Drizzle and Prisma. Their query, migration and transaction APIs belong to those libraries.
tradeoffs: Review eager loading, query counts and transaction semantics for the selected driver. Schema migrations, transactions and encrypted fields are compared separately.

migrations.note: The database guide points to external libraries such as Drizzle and Prisma. Their query, migration and transaction APIs belong to those libraries.
migrations.label: Drizzle / Prisma

transactions.note: The database guide points to external libraries such as Drizzle and Prisma. Their query, migration and transaction APIs belong to those libraries.
transactions.label: Drizzle / Prisma

jobs.note: The reviewed TanStack Start server/data guides do not establish an owned background jobs API. An application can integrate a separate provider or library; this finding does not mean that integration is impossible.

mail.note: The reviewed TanStack Start server/data guides do not establish an owned email API. An application can integrate a separate provider or library; this finding does not mean that integration is impossible.

uploads.note: Routes can read Request.formData and receive uploads. A framework storage lifecycle or upload service is not established.
uploads.label: Multipart endpoints

realtime.note: The reviewed TanStack Start server/data guides do not establish an owned real-time delivery API. An application can integrate a separate provider or library; this finding does not mean that integration is impossible.

xssEscaping.note: Its integrated UI renderer supplies this policy. Normal text values are rendered as text; dangerouslySetInnerHTML bypasses this path and requires trusted/sanitized HTML. Do not infer arbitrary URL/CSS safety from text escaping.

htmlSanitization.note: The linked security API review does not establish the specific html sanitization contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

authorization.note: The linked security API review does not establish the specific authorization policies contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

rateLimiting.note: The linked security API review does not establish the specific rate limiting contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

progressiveEnhancement.note: The server-functions guide documents native HTML forms using a server function’s .url. Return an appropriate Response/redirect and validate the request on the server. A JavaScript-only event handler is a different submission path.
progressiveEnhancement.label: Server-function URL forms

optimisticUi.note: React useOptimistic overlays pending mutation UI and reconciles against the supplied confirmed state through Actions/transitions. Application code must define the update and failure feedback; this is not a durable offline write queue.
optimisticUi.label: React useOptimistic

requestCancellation.note: Router loaders receive an AbortController that is canceled when a load is superseded. Loaders must pass its signal into cancelable I/O; server mutations are not rolled back by aborting the browser request.
requestCancellation.label: Loader abortController

typedLinks.note: TanStack Router checks route paths, params and navigation destinations from the registered route tree. The registration/type pipeline is required; casting a string can bypass its checks.
typedLinks.label: TanStack Router

searchParams.note: validateSearch parses/validates URL state into typed search values, with schema adapters and explicit malformed-input fallbacks/errors. TypeScript annotations alone are not runtime validation.
searchParams.label: validateSearch

stateRestoration.note: Persistent nested route components retain parent state while child matches change. Unmounted page state is not a general snapshot service; application/URL state is needed where retention is required.
stateRestoration.label: Nested route retention

scrollRestoration.note: Router scroll restoration tracks document and registered scrollable regions and restores before paint. scrollRestoration must be enabled; cache keys and virtualized scrollers may require configuration.
scrollRestoration.label: TanStack Router

navigationBlocking.note: useBlocker/Blocker can pause navigation for custom confirmation and provide proceed/reset. beforeunload covers browser exits separately and inherits browser restrictions.
navigationBlocking.label: TanStack Router

navigationAccessibility.note: The linked client rendering API review does not establish the specific accessible navigation contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

a11yChecks.note: The linked client rendering API review does not establish the specific accessibility checks contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

codeSplitting.note: The Router build integration automatically splits route components and noncritical exports while leaving matching-critical work available. Correct bundler/plugin configuration and shared chunks affect the output.
codeSplitting.label: Router build plugin
